journals.JAIS: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

themes.zh: AI 治理與負責任 AI

items.title: Computational Creativity in the AI Era: A Research Agenda for Information Systems
items.note: The guest editors define creativity as an instrumentable process of search, recombination, evaluation and realization, and position computational creativity as a durable IS research program.
items.authors: Min Ding, Ram Gopal, Ulrike Schultze, D. J. Wu

items.title: Inventing with Machines: Generative AI and the Evolving Landscape of IS Research
items.note: The editors argue GenAI changes not only how research is done but what research can be, and that IS is positioned to pioneer inventing with machines.
items.authors: Ram D. Gopal, Jingjing Li, Kai Riemer, Suprateek Sarker, Param Vir Singh, Anjana Susarla, Martin Bichler, Jason Bennett Thatcher

items.title: Digital Development: Reimagining Research Beyond ICT4D
items.note: The editorial replaces the ICT4D framing with digital development, treating digital and development trajectories as a duality across three dimensions.
items.authors: Sundeep Sahay, Shirish C. Srivastava, Michael Barrett, Robert M. Davison, Shirin Madon, Daniel Schlagwein, Irwin Brown, Suprateek Sarker

items.title: Advancing Next-Generation Multimethod Research in Information Systems: A Framework and Some Recommendations for Authors and Evaluators
items.note: The editors endorse multimethod research and propose a framework crossing methodological distance (proximate or distant) with nature of integration (interlayered or intertwined), yielding assembly, blend, bridge and fusion designs.
items.authors: Suprateek Sarker, Hillol Bala, Yili Hong, Atreyi Kankanhalli, Matti Rossi, Bin Gu, Gal Oestreicher-Singer

items.title: Human-Centric Information Systems Research on the Digital Future of Healthcare
items.note: Using topic modeling on 192 papers, the editors map six past themes and four emerging clusters in healthcare IS research.
items.authors: Indranil Bardhan, Rajiv Kohli, Eivor Oborn, Abhay Mishra, Chuan Hoo Tan, Monica Chiarini Tremblay, Suprateek Sarker

items.title: Engaging with Practice for Impactful Research
items.note: Third editorial of the 50th anniversary volume, co-authored by the EIC and eight senior editors.
items.authors: Susan A. Brown, Stefan Seidel, John D'Arcy, Jungpil Hahn, Carol Hsu, Sabine Matook, Maytal Saar-Tsechansky, Maha Shaikh, Jason Bennett Thatcher

items.title: The Evolution of Research in MIS Quarterly Over Five Decades
items.note: Brown reviews the 1,963 papers published in MISQ's first 50 years to trace how topics, methods and contributions evolved.
items.authors: Susan A. Brown

items.title: A Journey Through 50 Years of MIS Quarterly
items.note: Brown opens the anniversary volume by tracing the journal's 160 editorials and the parallel growth of the MIS discipline.
items.authors: Susan A. Brown

items.title: The Evolution of Social Media Networks: Revisiting and Extending Kane et al. (2014) 10 Years Later
items.note: The award winners revisit their 2014 framework classifying social media networks and ask which parts have held up.
items.authors: Gerald C. Kane, Maryam Alavi, Giuseppe (Joe) Labianca, Stephen P. Borgatti

items.title: Beyond Green IT: From Digital Sustainability to Responsible Technology
items.note: The EIC's December 2025 editorial, by its title, broadens the sustainability agenda from Green IT through digital sustainability to responsible technology.
items.authors: Susan A. Brown

items.title: Rebalancing Novelty with Rigor and Relevance in Information Systems Research
items.note: The editors argue novelty has become the dominant yardstick yet is inconsistently defined.
items.authors: Heshan Sun, Wen Wen, Jason Bennett Thatcher, Michael Chau, Susan A. Brown

items.title: Global by Design: Reaffirming Our Commitment to Inclusive IS Scholarship
items.note: The EIC and a senior editor reaffirm MISQ's commitment to globally inclusive scholarship.
items.authors: Michelle Carter, Susan A. Brown

items.title: Quantitative Behavioral IS Research: A Look Back and a Look Forward
items.note: A 16-page programmatic editorial by five senior editors and the EIC taking stock of quantitative behavioral IS research and charting its future.
items.authors: Likoebe M. Maruping, Dezhi Yin, Adela Chen, Atreyi Kankanhalli, Andrew Burton-Jones, Susan A. Brown

items.title: "Complexity Is the Worst Enemy of Security": Studying Cybersecurity Through the Lens of Organizational Complexity
items.note: The authors extend the principle that complexity is the worst enemy of security from software to organizations, where more components and interactions enlarge the attack surface and weaken accountability.
items.authors: Bruce Schneier, Anthony Vance

items.title: Editorial Introduction (43:3)
items.note: Zwass opens with open knowledge platforms as drivers of innovation, then foregrounds the human-GenAI interaction stream: how interaction modes and user reflection affect LLM factuality, how GenAI changes developers' code quality and cognitive effort, and how chatbot humanness suppresses error attribution.
items.authors: Vladimir Zwass

items.title: Editorial Introduction (43:2)
items.note: Zwass identifies a decisive shift in the field's objects of study toward human-AI collaboration, GenAI embedded in organizational processes, and platforms.
items.authors: Vladimir Zwass

items.title: Editorial Introduction (43:1)
items.note: Opening volume 43, Zwass argues leading journals must actively foster future-oriented research shaped by what is emerging in industry labs and startups.
items.authors: Vladimir Zwass

items.title: Editorial Introduction (42:4)
items.note: Zwass frames the issue around recommender systems and the dark side of engagement-driven media recommendation.
items.authors: Vladimir Zwass

items.title: Editorial Introduction (42:3)
items.note: Zwass devotes the editorial to free speech and asks where its boundaries lie in the age of social media and GenAI.
items.authors: Vladimir Zwass

items.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
items.note: The guest editors argue GenAI is a turning point for digital platforms because it reshapes value creation, participation and governance.
items.authors: Michael Wessel, Martin Adam, Alexander Benlian, Ann Majchrzak, Ferdinand Thies

items.title: Editorial Introduction (42:2)
items.note: Zwass characterizes digital platforms as the prevailing architecture of the online economy and connects GenAI job crafting to the vision of human-computer symbiosis.
items.authors: Vladimir Zwass

items.title: Long Live the Metaverse: Identifying the Potential for Market Disruption and Future Research
items.note: The guest editors contend the Metaverse is nascent rather than dead and is passing through the usual hype cycle, with GenAI likely to enable many Metaverse applications.
items.authors: Paul Benjamin Lowry, Wai Fong Boh, Stacie Petter, Jan Marco Leimeister

items.title: Editorial Introduction (42:1)
items.note: Zwass argues leading journals define the field's intellectual content and must shape it rather than merely filter.
items.authors: Vladimir Zwass

items.title: Fighting Fire with Fire: Infusing Artificial Intelligence into Peer Review to Sustain Quality Scholarship
items.note: The authors argue GenAI-driven submission growth pushes journals toward a capacity cliff, while shadow AI use by reviewers already creates correlated errors and confidentiality risks.
items.authors: Hemant K. Bhargava, Sarah H. Bana, Zhe Zhang, Laura Brandimarte, Vidyanand Choudhary, J. Frank Li, Pantelis Loupos, Daniel Zantedeschi

items.title: Introduction to the Special Issue on the Human-Algorithm Connection
items.note: The editors frame the issue around how humans and algorithms coexist and improve decision making together.
items.authors: Felipe Caro, Jean-Edouard Colliard, Elena Katok, Axel Ockenfels, Nicolas Stier-Moses, Catherine Tucker, D. J. Wu

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Operations: A Foundational Framework of Emerging Research and Practice
items.note: The authors argue AI's operational impact is a jagged implementation frontier with context-dependent, slow-to-appear benefits.
items.authors: Tinglong Dai, Jayashankar M Swaminathan

items.title: Internet of Things in Intralogistics: Applications and Emerging Research
items.note: The guest editors argue intralogistics decisions have rested on infrequent historical data, while IoT now delivers granular real-time data enabling dynamic decisions.
items.authors: René de Koster, Debjit Roy, Yun Fong Lim, Subodha Kumar

items.title: Embracing contrarian thinking: value-reflexive research for a better world
items.note: The guest editors argue scientific progress depends on contrarian thinking because unexamined assumptions lock in research trajectories.
items.authors: Markus Philipp Zimmer, Polyxeni Vassilakopoulou, Miria Grisot, Marko Niemimaa

items.title: Responsible AI starts with the artifact: Challenging the concept of responsible AI in IS research
items.note: The editors note a flood of AI submissions framed around responsibility.
items.authors: Patrick Mikalef, Alexander Benlian, Kieran Conboy, Monideepa Tarafdar

items.title: Positionality and Transparency: Rethinking Neutrality in Authorship and Reviewing
items.note: The EIC and co-authors question the assumption that authors and reviewers are neutral and argue for making researcher positionality transparent in authorship and peer review.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison, Miriam Klöpper, Dag Svanæs, Hameed Chughtai

items.title: Being Inclusive: Facets of ISJ's Reality
items.note: The EIC and two senior editors describe how inclusiveness plays out across ISJ's authors, reviewers, board and topics, continuing earlier editorials on diversity.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison, Angsana A. Techatassanasoontorn, Silvia Masiero

items.title: Research Integrity Matters, But It Is Undermined by Generative AI
items.note: The editors argue misuse of GAI is a growing cause of integrity violations and oppose its use for any intellectual activity of research, from brainstorming to drafting responses to reviewers.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison, Antonio Díaz Andrade, Andreas Eckhardt, Marjolein van Offenbeek, Angsana A. Techatassanasoontorn, Marco Marabelli, Petter Nielsen, Niki Panteli, Gerhard Schwabe, Andrew Hardin, Vanessa Cooper

items.title: Scholarly Integrity and Generative AI: Five Boundary Violations for IS Scholarship
items.note: The authors identify five ways GAI use crosses boundaries of scholarly integrity in IS research.
items.authors: Jonny Holmström, Robert M. Davison

items.title: The Art of Crafting an Enticing Opening Gambit
items.note: A two-page EIC editorial in the craft-of-writing series on how a paper's opening should hook editors, reviewers and readers.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison

items.title: Generative AI Is Neither Just Another IT Artefact nor a Colleague: Methodological Guidance for IS Scholarship
items.note: The editors note GAI submissions have surged while treatment of the GAI artefact is often superficial.
items.authors: Kai Riemer, Sandra Peter, Gerhard Schwabe, Sutirtha Chatterjee, Martin Adam, Robert M. Davison

items.title: Information Systems in and for Practice
items.note: An editorial introducing ISJ's practice-oriented paper stream, following the 2023 practitioner-perspective editorial and call.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison, Marco Marabelli, Yenni Tim

items.title: The Future (As a Focus) of IS Research
items.note: The EIC and a senior editor argue the future itself should become a focus of IS research, related to the futures studies call.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison, Gerhard Schwabe

items.title: Why You Should Write a Cover Letter
items.note: A two-page EIC note urging a substantive cover letter with each submission.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison

items.title: Digital Transformation: Quo Vadit?
items.note: The guest editors examine how the digital transformation concept has evolved and argue for a more nuanced understanding.
items.authors: Lauri Wessel, Elaine Mosconi, Marta Indulska, Abayomi Baiyere

items.title: Decoloniality and Information Systems: Making Local Contexts Relevant to IS Research
items.note: Guest editorial for the decoloniality special issue, arguing for making local, non-Western contexts and knowledges relevant to IS research.
items.authors: Hameed Chughtai, Amber G. Young

items.title: Exploring Alternative (Non-Economic) Forms of Value Engendered by Digital Platforms
items.note: Special issue introduction on non-economic forms of value created through digital platforms, beyond platform economics.
items.authors: Petros Chamakiotis, Dimitra Petrakaki

items.title: Reviews, recommendations and decisions: Contrasting perspectives
items.note: The EIC contrasts how reviewer reports, editor recommendations and EIC decisions can diverge and how authors should read them.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison

items.title: The new wave of 'hybrid' work: An opportunity to revise assumptions and build theory
items.note: The guest editors argue hybrid work demands fresh thinking about how space, time and technology interact, and challenge treating technology as a black box or neutral enabler.
items.authors: Efpraxia D. Zamani, Mary Beth Watson-Manheim, Pamela Abbott, Angela Lin

items.title: Digitally enabled sharing economy models at the base of the pyramid
items.note: Guest editors' editorial for the special issue on digitally enabled sharing economy models at the base of the pyramid.
items.authors: Israr Qureshi, Babita Bhatt, Dhirendra Mani Shukla

items.title: The Dynamics, Organisation and Evolution of Digital Platforms and Ecosystems
items.note: The guest editors organise the special issue around how ecosystem entities compete and collaborate, how different types organise for success, and how ecosystems emerge and evolve.
items.authors: Barney Tan, Xiao Xiao, Michael Chau, Felix Ter Chian Tan, Carmen Leong

items.title: Information systems and sustainable development: From conceptual underpinnings to empirical insights
items.note: Three-page special issue introduction on how IS help achieve the UN SDGs, including critical perspectives.
items.authors: Barney Tan, Petter Nielsen

items.title: Fit, scope and the shifting baseline: Is your submission likely to be desk rejected?
items.note: The EIC and two senior editors explain desk rejection in terms of fit with scope and a shifting baseline of expected contribution.
items.authors: Robert M. Davison, Stan Karanasios, Sutirtha Chatterjee

items.title: Digital Sustainability and Information Systems Research: Emerging Perspectives and Future Directions
items.note: The guest editors find growing but thematically narrow sustainability research, still mostly environmental.
items.authors: Julia Kotlarsky, Jacqueline Corbett, Juliana Sutanto, Thomas Kude, Yenni Tim

items.title: Writing an "A" Paper in the Age of GenAI: A Guide to Responsible Augmentation
items.note: An editorial guide on how authors can use GenAI to augment rather than replace scholarly writing responsibly, including worked example prompts.
items.authors: Gerald C. Kane, Monideepa Tarafdar

items.title: The Changing Landscape of Behavioral IS Research: Navigating Agentic, Epistemic, and Cognitive Shifts
items.note: The authors argue AI reshapes behavioral IS research through agentic, epistemic and cognitive shifts.
items.authors: Varun Grover, Monideepa Tarafdar

items.title: Expanding the Scope of IS Research Impact: A Framework and Guidelines
items.note: The authors treat impact as a multifaceted construct spanning academia, business and society, and propose a framework plus guidelines for planning, delivering, measuring and communicating it.
items.authors: Hind Benbya, Mareike Möhlmann, Jan vom Brocke

items.title: Theorizing From Contexts in Research With Digital Trace Data
items.note: Vaast argues digital trace data are themselves part of the contexts studied, creating a tension between staying close to context and rushing to theory.
items.authors: Emmanuelle Vaast

items.title: Going Beyond "Our Research Also Has Policy Implications..."
items.note: The editors argue IS policy research should make policy the central object of study rather than an appended implications paragraph.
items.authors: Roman Beck, Monideepa Tarafdar, Aaron Cheng, John L. King, Fred Niederman

items.title: Information Systems Research for Policy Impact: A Systemic View From the Trenches
items.note: A short companion to the Beck et al.
items.authors: Monideepa Tarafdar, Ritu Agarwal, Ramayya Krishnan

items.title: Digital Responsibility: Current Perspectives and Future Directions
items.note: The editors define digital responsibility through accountability, an obligation to pursue good outcomes while guarding against harm, and dependability as a sustained commitment.
items.authors: Jan Recker, Sutirtha Chatterjee, Janina Sundermeier, Monideepa Tarafdar

items.title: Journal of the Association for Information Systems, 25 Years In: Letting a Thousand Flowers Bloom and Keeping the Fences
items.note: The anniversary editorial describes JAIS as deliberately open across topics, levels, theories and methods, and assesses 2019 to 2024 papers to chart future narratives.
items.authors: Monideepa Tarafdar, Hui Hao, Guohou Shan

items.title: Health Analytics and IS Theorizing
items.note: The guest editors show how IS researchers can make theoretical contributions in health analytics and propose directions including causal ML for hypothesis generation, fairness in resource allocation, human-AI collaboration in care processes and policy learning.
items.authors: Aaron Baird, Yusen Xia, Rajiv Kohli

items.title: Policy for Sociotechnical Gen AI Assessment: Leveraging End Users
items.note: The authors argue GenAI assessment must be sociotechnical and recommend treating end users as a key knowledge source, offering an illustrative framework.
items.authors: Ju Yeon Jung, Susan J. Winter

items.title: Legal Compliance and the Open Texture of Law
items.note: The authors argue laws are often vague, so compliance requires interpretation before compliance mechanisms can be designed and must proceed under uncertainty.
items.authors: Arto Lanamäki, Mika Viljanen, Karin Väyrynen, Lyria Bennett Moses

items.title: The future of information systems in the enterprise
items.note: The guest editors argue enterprise IS should be studied at the level of the enterprise as evolving systems of systems, using lenses of coherency, tensions and integration mechanisms.
items.authors: Robert Winter, Leona Chandra Kruse, Rajiv Sabherwal, Karlheinz Kautz

items.title: From 'ChatGPT et al.' to generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in peer review: Safeguarding trust while modernising scholarly publishing
items.note: The editors argue GenAI in peer review must be governed rather than ignored.
items.authors: Jan Marco Leimeister, Aleksi Aaltonen, Wendy Currie, Daniel Schlagwein

items.title: Prediction, hype, and fear: Advancing Information Systems research in "the AI age"
items.note: The EICs argue IS should engage systematically with digital futures using methods for reasoning under uncertainty, treat hype as a legitimate research object, and use AI as a critical test case through capability, adoption, value and consequence lenses.
items.authors: Leslie Willcocks, Wendy Currie, Daniel Schlagwein, Jan Marco Leimeister

items.title: From ideology to design: Toward purposeful decentralization of information systems governance
items.note: The guest editors propose a (De)centralization Dynamics Pendulum and argue decentralisation should be a design and governance choice, not an ideology.
items.authors: Ali Sunyaev, Michel Avital, Mary C. Lacity

items.title: Rethinking technology regulation in the age of AI risks
items.note: The editors argue AI exposes the limits of general legal principles and demands risk-informed, technology-specific governance.
items.authors: Wendy L Currie, Jan Marco Leimeister, Daniel Schlagwein, Leslie Willcocks

items.title: Next-generation IS research methods: towards a better understanding of complex and dynamic phenomena ... and generative AI as the elephant in the room
items.note: The guest editors argue IS needs methods that capture complex, dynamic and temporal phenomena, and that GenAI is an unavoidable productivity aid across paradigms.
items.authors: Ivo Blohm, Shaila Miranda, Shuk Ying Ho, Jan Marco Leimeister

items.title: Organizing vision revisited and reimagined for a changing world
items.note: The authors revisit organizing vision theory, find it applied to about 46 technologies but confined mostly to IS, and ask whether AI challenges it.
items.authors: E Burton Swanson, Neil Ramiller, Ping Wang

items.title: Digital futures: Definition (what), importance (why) and methods (how)
items.note: The editors propose digital futures as a research field studying diverse long-term futures shaped by digital technologies, defined pluralistically.
items.authors: Daniel Schlagwein, Wendy Currie, Jan Marco Leimeister, Leslie Willcocks

items.title: Literature reviews on emerging technologies: The role of grey literature
items.note: Editorial for the 2026 review issue by the four Review Issue editors.
items.authors: Marco Marabelli, Tuure Tuunanen, Wenyu Derek Du, Rohit Nishant

items.title: Welcome to the third issue of Volume 35 of the Journal of Strategic Information Systems
items.note: Co-EIC introduction to the 2026 review issue.
items.authors: Benoit A. Aubert, Rajiv Sabherwal

items.title: Welcome to the second issue of Volume 35 of the Journal of Strategic Information Systems
items.note: Co-EIC introduction to the issue carrying the digital transformation and work special issue.
items.authors: Rajiv Sabherwal, Benoit A. Aubert

items.title: Digital transformation as future-ready strategizing: beyond the destination view
items.note: Guest editors' piece arguing for digital transformation as ongoing future-ready strategizing rather than a destination.
items.authors: Abayomi Baiyere, Ioanna Constantiou, Marta Indulska, Virpi Kristiina Tuunainen

items.title: Welcome to the first issue of Volume 35 of the Journal of Strategic Information Systems
items.note: Co-EIC introduction to a regular issue.
items.authors: Benoit A. Aubert, Rajiv Sabherwal

items.title: Are immersive platforms the future of work? The role of generative AI and DEI considerations
items.note: Special issue editorial asking how immersive platforms could enable new work practices while raising ethical and DEI pitfalls, with GenAI added as a reshaping force.
items.authors: Marco Marabelli, Sue Newell, Manju Ahuja, Bob Galliers

items.title: Welcome to the fourth issue of Volume 34 of the Journal of Strategic Information Systems
items.note: Co-EIC introduction to the immersive platforms special issue.
items.authors: Rajiv Sabherwal, Benoit A. Aubert

items.title: Special issues at JSIS: Past, present and future (guidelines for prospective guest editors)
items.note: The special issues coordinator reviews JSIS's history with special issues and sets out guidelines for prospective guest editors.
items.authors: Marco Marabelli, Joel José Rivera Jimenez

items.title: Welcome to the third issue of volume 34 of the Journal of Strategic Information Systems
items.note: First issue editorial by the new co-EICs after succeeding Yolande Chan.
items.authors: Benoit A. Aubert, Rajiv Sabherwal

items.title: Artificial intelligence and the environment: ethical challenges and strategic opportunities for organizations
items.note: The viewpoint raises awareness of GenAI's environmental footprint and argues its benefits accrue to the Global North while the Global South bears disproportionate harm.
items.authors: Marco Marabelli, Robert M. Davison

items.title: AI Agents: Potential implications for IS Research?
items.note: Editorial for the 2025 review issue asking what agentic AI means for IS research.
items.authors: Shan Ling Pan, Rohit Nishant, Tuure Tuunanen, Jyoti Choudrie

items.title: Welcome to the second issue of Volume 34 of the Journal of Strategic Information Systems
items.note: The outgoing EIC's last issue editorial, introducing the 2025 review issue.
items.authors: Yolande E. Chan

items.title: Welcome to the first issue of Volume 34 of the Journal of Strategic Information Systems
items.note: EIC introduction to a regular issue.
items.authors: Yolande E. Chan

items.title: Editorial for the special issue: Empowering bright internet and bright AI
items.note: Introduces the special issue applying Bright Internet principles of preventive threat mitigation to AI, covering AI governance, privacy and cybersecurity, fairness, transparency, trust and accountability.
items.authors: Daegon Cho, Shan Liu, Dan J. Kim

items.title: Metaverse opportunities and challenges: A research agenda and editorial on the special issue on the evolution of Metaverse platforms (part 2)
items.note: The editors treat the metaverse as a distinct IT artifact with its own research directions and propose a layered framework from technology artifacts through techno-functional features and adoption to impacts on individuals, organizations and societies.
items.authors: Arpan Kumar Kar, Patrick Mikalef, Rohit Nishant, Xin (Robert) Luo, Manish Gupta

items.title: Returning the "socio" to decision support research: Expanding beyond a purely technical mindset
items.note: The authors argue design-science decision support research is too technical, illustrate with the 1854 cholera investigations, and contend socio-technical design artifacts are effectively discouraged at DSS.
items.authors: Cecil Eng Huang Chua, Fred Niederman

items.title: The evolution of organizations and stakeholders for metaverse ecosystems: Editorial for the special issue on metaverse part 1
items.note: The editors argue platforms are evolving into metaverse ecosystems while empirical research on their socio-technical aspects remains limited.
items.authors: Arpan Kumar Kar, Patrick Mikalef, Rohit Nishant, Xin (Robert) Luo, Manish Gupta

items.title: Agentic artificial intelligence as a new frontier in information systems: Promise, peril, and research opportunities
items.note: The authors argue agentic AI is a new frontier for IS research and take a socio-technical stance in which tensions around displacement, transparency, governance and equity are structural consequences of how agentic systems interact with roles and institutions.
items.authors: Naveen Kumar, Xiahua Wei, Han Zhang

items.title: Navigating digital turbulence and seizing new possibilities: Special issue from the Pacific Asia Conference on Information Systems
items.note: Guest editors' editorial for the PACIS 2023 special issue.
items.authors: Andrew Burton-Jones, Chuan-Hoo Tan, Bo (Justin) Xiao

items.title: Addressing bias in generative AI: Challenges and research opportunities in information management
items.note: The authors trace GenAI bias to training data, algorithmic assumptions and human subjectivity, review detection and debiasing methods, and propose a framework spanning research design, technical development and policy impact.
items.authors: Xiahua Wei, Naveen Kumar, Han Zhang

items.title: Platform governance as institutional custodianship: multi-actor collaboration in combating AI-enabled mis/disinformation
items.note: The editors argue platforms bear significant responsibility for curbing AI-enabled false content and that governance must maintain institutional trust.
items.authors: Michael Barrett, Isam Faik, Tawfik Jelassi

items.title: Digital innovation, platforms, and global strategy
items.note: Guest editors' introduction to the special issue on digital innovation, platforms and global strategy.
items.authors: Danielle M. Logue, Peter J. Williamson, Anna Elise Roberts, Yadong Luo, Michael Barrett
